# Google Search's Guidance on Using Generative AI Content on Your Website

Source: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/using-gen-ai-content

Google advises that while generative AI can help with research and structuring content, creating many pages without adding user value may breach spam policies. The guidance emphasizes that AI-generated work must meet Search Essentials standards.

## Key Requirements

**Accuracy and Quality Matter**: Content creators should prioritize accuracy, quality, and relevance, particularly for automatically generated material. This includes metadata elements like titles, descriptions, structured data, and image alt text that appear in search results.

**Transparency Is Valuable**: Google recommends disclosing how content was created. As stated in their guidance, sharing "information about how a piece of content was created" helps readers understand the role of automation in production.

**Ecommerce Specifics**: For product listings, Google Merchant Center requires AI-generated images to include IPTC metadata marking them as algorithmically produced, and AI-generated product descriptions must be clearly labeled as such.

## Enforcement Context

Google's Search Quality Raters use guidelines evaluating scaled content abuse and low-effort content lacking originality. These ratings help assess ranking systems but don't directly determine rankings themselves.

## Overarching Principle

AI can be a useful tool, but outputs must deliver genuine value to users and comply with anti-spam policies regarding automated, low-quality content generation.
